hints: Focus on what the fifth ionisation energy actually removes, so write out the electron arrangements of Al and P first.
Count off the electrons removed one by one, Al has only 3 outer electrons in n=3 while P has 5.
Recall the Period 3 oxide trend from basic to amphoteric to acidic, and place Al2O3 and phosphorus oxides on it.
walkthrough:
**Write the electron configurations**

Both elements are in Period 3, so think about the n=3 outer shell.

$$\text{Al (13): } 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1$$
$$\text{P (15): } 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3$$

**Track the first five removals**

For Al, the first 3 removals clear the n=3 shell. The 4th removal must break into the n=2 inner shell.

For P, the first 3 removals clear the $3p$ electrons, and the 4th and 5th removals clear the $3s$ electrons. All five are still from n=3.

**Compare the 5th ionisation energy**

Removing an inner shell electron needs much more energy because it is closer to the nucleus and less shielded.

So the 5th ionisation energy of Al (from $2p$) is far greater than the 5th of P (from $3s$).

**Check the oxide character**

Across Period 3, oxides change from basic to amphoteric to acidic.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 \text{ is amphoteric, } \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} \text{ is acidic}$$ 
Only aluminium has an amphoteric oxide, so the correct row is aluminium and aluminium only.

options.A: Correct. Al has the greater 5th ionisation energy because its 5th electron comes from the n=2 inner shell, while P's 5th electron still comes from n=3. And only Al2O3 is amphoteric, phosphorus oxides are acidic.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. Aluminium does have the greater 5th ionisation energy, but phosphorus does not form an amphoteric oxide. Its oxides, P4O6 and P4O10, are acidic and react with bases only.
options.C: The oxide part is right, but the ionisation energy is reversed. Students choose this by thinking more protons means higher successive ionisation energy, forgetting that Al has already broken into the inner shell by the 5th removal while P has not.
options.D: Both parts are incorrect. P has the lower 5th ionisation energy because it is still removing n=3 electrons, and its oxide is acidic, not amphoteric. This confuses the big jump positions for Al (between 3rd and 4th) and P (between 5th and 6th).
